rationale: Plasma was run in two acquisition batches, and batch shifts in protein intensity get mixed into the pooled AUROC. I'm centring each protein's log2 values on its median within each batch. This is label-free harmonization and should help the regularized linear model separate AD from controls instead of batch. Caveat: if the AD/control ratio differs a lot between batches, centring could also remove some real signal.

The plasma samples were run in two acquisition batches and are scored pooled, so batch-level intensity shifts per protein can swamp or distort the AD signal across samples. This version subtracts each protein's median within each batch, using the observed values and no labels, before imputation and the L2 logistic model. I haven't run it, so its effect on the 0.8935 dev score is unknown.

The plasma samples were run in two acquisition batches. Batch shifts in each protein's log intensity add noise that has nothing to do with AD, so I'm centring every protein within its batch. Only the training fold sets the per-batch medians, which also handle imputed values. Test samples get their own batch's training median, or the overall training median if that batch is missing from the training fold. Labels are never used.

I'll centre each protein on its median within each batch (label-free, done in featurize on the observed values) so the regularized logistic model learns disease signal instead of batch offsets. With a pooled half-minimum fill and pooled scaling, that offset becomes noise the classifier has to work around. This change subtracts each protein's per-batch median of the log2 values, computed on the observed values only, before imputation. It never looks at labels and uses batch only to harmonize, so the AD-vs-control contrast within each batch should come through more cleanly.

Plasma DIA intensities carry strong batch effects across the two acquisition batches, and the L2 logistic model can pick these up as noise or confounding. I'm adding a per-batch, per-protein median centring step, label-free and done in `featurize` on log2 values using only observed values. It's a standard harmonization and should make protein levels comparable between batches. This is untested: if AD and control samples are split unevenly across batches, centring could also remove some real signal, so the CV score will show which effect wins.

The plasma data were acquired in two batches, and the score is pooled across them. Any shift in protein level between batches therefore adds noise to the ranking, or creates a shortcut that won't carry over to new data. I'm adding one change: after the per-sample median centring, each protein's log2 values are median-centred within each batch. This is label-free and uses only the batch metadata, which the brief allows for harmonization.

The two DIA acquisition batches probably shift protein intensities, and that adds noise the classifier can't remove. This change centres each protein on its median within each batch, after log2 transformation and per-sample median centring. It uses only the batch labels, never the outcome, so it is allowed harmonization, and it puts both batches on the same scale before filtering, imputation and the L2-regularized logistic regression.
